sample_unit: board-exam cases (converted to 24-slot records and simulated dialogues)
models_evaluated: fifteen LLM doctor agents (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLM doctor agents across simulated patient personas by education level
links.effect: Patient persona differences shifted diagnosis accuracy by about 7-8 points from lowest to highest education, indicating equity risks.
links.quote: (iii) patient persona differences can shift diagnosis accuracy by about 7-8 points (lowest to highest education), highlighting equity risks that single-turn benchmarks miss.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy drop from single-turn benchmark to multi-turn consultation
links.effect: Moving from single-turn diagnosis to multi-turn consultations caused degradations of roughly 13-39 points, showing single-turn benchmarks overstate competence.
links.quote: (i) moving from a single-turn diagnosis on the standardized records to multi-turn consultations causes large degradations of roughly 13-39 points

unlisted_practices: Difficulty-stratified evaluation of diagnostic AI using model-based uncertainty
Evaluating multi-turn information-seeking (question relevance and turn count) of AI doctor agents

screen.reason: The paper introduces and evaluates a multi-turn doctor-patient LLM benchmark (MedRoundsQA) to evaluate diagnostic accuracy across turns and patient personas; it does not test a health system deployment practice or operational safeguard.
